title: Four Potential Replacements for USMNT Boss Pochettino Amid Man Utd Links
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia Vesely6:00 PM ESTMauricio Pochettino could be on his way out. /  Omar Vega/Getty ImagesU.S. men’s national team manager Mauricio Pochettino could be headed for the exit door, emerging as a frontrunner to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United upon the return of Premier League action following the November international break.

After commanding the Red Devils to just one Premier League win across the first 10 matches of the new season—and seeing the club drop into the relegation zone for the first time in 40 years, Carrick finds himself on the chopping block, reportedly set to be fired within the coming hours or days.

Pochettino is currently under contract in the States through the 2030 World Cup; however, his deal reportedly includes a buyout clause worth around $10 million, a sum United may be just desperate enough to pay.
The Argentine boss, formerly at the helms of Paris Saint-Germain, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, has been honest about his “ambition” to return to the club level.

“We are still young, and I think coming back is always my goal,” the 54-year-old said in September. “To win the Premier League, to be in the Premier League and to build a project with the possibility of winning.
“I love the football here,” he added. “I think to have the chance again is one of my wishes and I hope that happens.”

If Pochettino is in fact on his way to the red side of Manchester, who could replace him at the helm of the USMNT? The Americans have strong ambitions for the 2030 World Cup, which would require a leader that can successfully build on the foundation Pochettino has laid.

B.J. Callaghan led Nashville SC to the best regular season in MLS history. / Jeff Dean/MLS/Getty ImagesOff the back of making Major League Soccer history, B.J. Callaghan could be an outside contender to replace Pochettino.
Callaghan extended his contract with Nashville SC through the 2028–29 season in February; however, U.S. Soccer may still be inclined to pry him away.

Not only does the 45-year-old out of Ventnor City, N.J. have experience with the USMNT—serving as the team’s interim manager back in 2023, he has also proven his managerial worth tenfold over the past two seasons in MLS.

2025 was his first full season in Nashville, and although the club did not win the MLS Cup that year, Callaghan still achieved several club records, including the most single-season wins (22 all competition) and the longest unbeaten streak (15 all competitions). He also led the Boys in Gold to their first-ever trophy: the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup.

His 2026 campaign has been even more prolific, establishing this Nashville squad as the single greatest regular season team in MLS history. They surpassed Inter Miami’s 2024 squad (74) for the highest points tally in MLS regular season history (77) and also set league records for most wins (23), fewest losses (3), points per game (2.26), win percentage (79.4), fewest goals conceded (25) and the largest Supporters’ Shield points margin (13).
It was total domination from Callaghan’s men, who seem destined to hoist their first-ever MLS Cup. Meanwhile, their manager could be headed out the door.
Julian Nagelsmann most recently managed Germany at the 2026 World Cup. / Michael Reaves/Getty ImagesJulian Nagelsmann could also be a worthwhile replacement for Pochettino.

The 39-year-old from West Germany most recently commanded the German national team at the 2026 World Cup, taking over at the helm in 2023 after stints as manager for TSG Hoffenheim (2016–19), RB Leipzig (2019–21) and Bayern Munich (2021–23).

He issued his resignation soon after Germany’s shock exit to Paraguay in the round of 32 last summer and has been a free agent ever since. Nagelsmann has shown an interest in returning to the club game; however, if U.S. Soccer comes calling, it may be too enticing of an offer to refuse.

It may not have worked wonders at Germany, but his managerial style on the surface is quite suitable to the USMNT’s style of play. The German boss is known for his tactical flexibility, which could be a strength for an American team still discovering its key players and most successful formation. He is also known for his aggressive pressing and counter attacking, a tactic that worked well at the World Cup for Pochettino, who has foregrounded an identity of aggressive front-footedness.

There is one potential red flag, though. Nagelsmann’s defense fell incredibly short at the World Cup, seeing Germany display a leaky backline throughout the entire tournament. It’s what ultimately led to the powerhouse’s early demise.
